chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a Christian who was called as a witness for a testimony, and then he embraced Islam afterwards. Is his testimony valid? He said, 'Yes, he is in the same position as his testimony.'

key_terms.مَوْضِعِ شَهَادَتِهِ: Position of his testimony / State of his witnessing

ai.seo_question: Does a witness's conversion to Islam invalidate their previous testimony given while they were Christian?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'stability of the state at the time of the act' (istishab al-hal), ruling that a Christian's testimony remains valid upon their conversion to Islam because the legal status at the moment of witnessing was sound. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for resolving disputes regarding the retroactive validity of actions performed by Ahl al-Kitab, emphasizing that the subsequent change in religious identity does not nullify the prior legal capacity. It highlights the pragmatic approach of the Imams in validating social transactions based on the witness's standing at the specific time of the event.
